title: fix: CI reports job and test time instead of failing on it
headline: A job or test over its time limit is reported, not failed, and a job over on 3 main runs in a row is named as a trend; the Windows tests run over 2 runners.
alignment: v1.51.3 is the fix that let 1.51.2 ship: main went red after its merge only because the Windows job ran 189 s against the 180 s limit. It brings K401 and K384 forward from 1.51.4, and the release carries 1.51.2 with it.

items.text: Job time and test time are reported, not failed: a job over 180 s on 3 main runs in a row is named as a trend for a list row, and the Windows 60 s cap is gone.
items.where: A PR whose job runs over 180 s
items.after: Reported; 3 main runs over make a trend
tests: tests/ci-budget.test.mjs::a job over the limit on 3 main runs in a row is named as a trend, and 2 in a row is not

items.text: The Windows tests run over 2 runners; the Windows test check and the guard proofs run once, on the first.

verification: The new trend test and the changed time tests failed on the code before them and pass now.
A failed, timed-out or unfinished job still fails the required check; only time is a report.

decisions.decision: Time is a report and a trend, not a gate
decisions.why: Runner speed alone made 7 of PR 71's 29 reds; the owner's yes (2026-11-23).
Main moved to 1.51.2 at the merge, and CI owes a VERSION move for this change; the owner's pick (2026-11-23).

upgrading: Run install project to take the report-only budget step in the CI templates; the kit's own CI changes need nothing.
limits: The trend reads only the 2 main runs before this one, so a job renamed by the Windows split starts its trend afresh. Projects get no trend line in CI yet; their lane report keeps its own 3-run check.

tests.flips: declared tests at main and on this branch; the PR run gives the final count
